title: NY AG Letitia James too ‘biased’ to fairly investigate ‘Cornell 7’ frat boys: critics
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
NY AG Letitia James too ‘biased’ to fairly investigate ‘Cornell 7’ frat boys: critics

New York Attorney General Letitia James is too political, biased and unethical to fairly investigate the seven Cornell University fraternity brothers accused of raping a female classmate, pols and other critics told The Post.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

New York Attorney General Letitia James is too political, biased and unethical to fairly investigate the seven Cornell University fraternity brothers accused of raping a female classmate, pols and other critics told The Post.

James had already posted sympathy for the accuser on social media days before Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed her Friday to be the special prosecutor in the exploding scandal — and now refuses to  comment on the biased remarks.

Rensselaer County Executive Steven McLaughlin — whom James indicted on grand larceny and election fraud charges in 2021 but was later acquitted by a jury – said the “Cornell Seven” should “expect the worst” because he’s living proof that the lefty Democratic prosecutor is “anything but impartial.”

“She’s clearly engaged in targeted persecutions and prosecutions,” the Republican pol said. “She targeted me. She targeted the president.

“In my case, she spent over $1 million trying to nail me over absolutely nothing. She is clearly engaged in targeted political hits. I don’t know all the facts of the case, but I am sure she is going to try and nail these guys rather than let justice prevail.”

McLaughlin joined a growing chorus of critics who agreed with President Trump, who predicted Friday the Cornell Seven won’t get a “fair shake” with James on the case — because the attorney general is a “corrupt person.”

James won a massive $454 million civil judgment against Trump’s business for allegedly inflating its value, but the decision was overturned by a state appeals court last year.

“Much like with the legal action she brought against the president, Attorney General Tish James appears to have already drawn her own conclusions about this incident, without gathering all the facts,” said City Councilman Frank Morano (R-Staten Island).

“I don’t know how anyone could expect her to be fair and objective.”

Council Minority Leader David Carr said James “has a well-documented history of making highly charged public statements about people she is investigating and prosecuting.

“That is exactly the wrong background for a special prosecutor in a case where impartiality is everything,” said the Staten Island Republican.

“She was publicly characterizing this case before she was even appointed. The allegations deserve to be investigated aggressively, but the accused also deserve due process.”

Melissa DeRosa, a former top aide to ex-Gov. Andrew Cuomo who has accused James of leading an unfair sexual harassment probe that spurred her Democratic boss’ 2021 resignation, also questioned the appointment.

“I think Kathy Hochul was trying to come up with a political solution to a media storm,” DeRosa said Friday  on Fox and Friends.

“Tish James is known to be highly political. Her track record in general is highly political, and I would argue in this instance in particular you need to go the other way and make sure what is being done is not about headline grabbing and not about politics but true to the law.”

Joe Giacalone, a retired NYPD sergeant and an adjunct professor at John Jay College of Criminal Justice, said he has “zero faith” in James “using discretion and using just the law to investigate the case.

“I think an independent outsider should have been appointed to do this,” he said. “That Facebook post was ridiculous.”

Hochul’s office did not return messages on Saturday, and James ducked questions about her role in the case during an unrelated Bronx event.

But Hochul on Friday told reporters she has “every confidence” in James “to do what she has always done: look at the facts, examine the record and draw the proper conclusions.”

“That’s exactly what’s going to happen in this case,” she said.

The case became national news when a “Jane Doe” defendant filed a lawsuit in Manhattan Supreme Court last month accusing seven fraternity brothers of raping her at the Cornell’s Phi Chi fraternity house in Oct
